newsitem.title: USA: COMEX COPPER DOWN AT MIDDAY ON FUND, BANK SELLING.
newsitem.headline: COMEX COPPER DOWN AT MIDDAY ON FUND, BANK SELLING.

text.p: COMEX copper fell at midday, breaking through trendline support at 105.00 cents a lb in the September contract and triggering light fund stops, brokers said.
The uptrend had dated back to July 9's low of 101.50 cents, but funds and a large U.K. bank started selling in conjunction with the late London kerb. Arbitrage dealers were buyers at the lows.
At 1232 EDT, active September was down 1.20 cents at 104.90 cents, traded 104.20 to 106.40 cents, with the spot month 1.05 cents lower at 104.80 cents.
"The longer we stay at these levels, the more selling we're likely to see from the funds," said one floor source.

Fundamentals took a back seat to the technicals. The LME cash-to-three-month backwardation contracted to $18/$23 from $28 at Friday's close. LME stocks increased another 1,700 tonnes to 250,400 tonnes in Monday's report.
The LME cash price was trading at approximately 0.50 cent over the COMEX spot price.
